messages:
alex: heads-up — noticed a short spike in quota burn for tenant t-42 between 17:22-17:27. streaming resume events spiked but active_session gauge stayed flat. looks tied to a sequence of pingbacks hitting the edge which then trigger resumes. anyone seen this pattern?
maya: i pulled the billing panel — resumed_count jumped ~3x for that tenant but connections didn't grow. billing looks like duplicate resume charges. :thinking_face:
jonathan: digging logs on edge-5. i see a repeating sequence where proxy receives a PINGBACK then immediately schedules a RESUME with same resume_id. snippet:
```
proxy: received PINGBACK session=abc resume_id=ri123 lease_age_ms=1200
proxy: schedule RESUME session=abc resume_id=ri123 attempt=1
```
sasha: that smells like lease splay + forwarding bug. pingback should be treated as keepalive, not a missed heartbeat. why would forwarder flip the semantics?
alex: my hunch: forwarded pingbacks increment last_seen at the origin but when the proxy processes a forwarded pingback it sets a different field and the resume decision path thinks last_seen is stale. replicated on edge-5 and edge-9.
infra-bot: alert created INC-2026-014 for quota-anomaly, linked dashboards and logs.
emily: console query for context: `sum(rate(stream_resume_total[1m])) by (region,tenant)` vs `sum(rate(stream_heartbeat_recv[1m]))`. the ratio is off — resumes >> heartbeats for the window. dashboard panel shows resume events under Errors which inflates SLA numbers.
jonathan: looking at code: resume decision is `if now - last_seen > lease_ttl then schedule_resume()`. forwarded pingback currently calls `bump_last_seen_forwarded()` which updates a different timestamp (`forwarded_last_seen`) but the resume check uses `last_seen`. race when both fields out of sync.
sasha: proposed mitigations: (1) treat forwarded pingbacks as idempotent and don't trigger resume without an explicit missed heartbeat; (2) add a short debounce window before resume scheduling; (3) change console labeling so resume control events don't count as user-facing errors.
maya: can we add instrumentation first? i want a metric `pingback_forwarded_total{edge,tenant}` and correlate with `stream_resume_total`. also capture `resume_reason` tag (heartbeat|pingback|auth).
alex: yes — add `forwarded` flag to the resume event and include original source ip. that'll make dashboards much clearer.
jonathan: i'll open a small PR to adjust the resume branch: only call schedule_resume() if (!forwarded && now - last_seen > ttl) || (forwarded && now - forwarded_last_seen > ttl + splay). quick patch + canary to edge-5. code snippet in PR: 
```
if (event.type == PINGBACK) {
  if (!event.forwarded) last_seen = now;
  else forwarded_last_seen = now;
}
if (now - last_seen > ttl && !event.forwarded) schedule_resume();
if (event.forwarded && now - forwarded_last_seen > ttl + splay) schedule_resume();
```
sasha: also UX ask: can we classify resume events as ControlTraffic so they don't show as Errors in the SLA panel? support gets confused by these spikes.
emily: agreed. i'll update the panel and add a comparison chart: resumes (control) vs resumes (user) so support can filter.
maya: rollout plan: patch + canary on edge-5 for 30m, monitor `pingback_forwarded_total` and `stream_resume_total` and billing delta. if clean, roll to global. add alert if resumes > 2% of connections for 5m.
alex: please also add a short note in runbook about expected billing blips and how to explain them to customers. support should be prepped.
jonathan: PR opened: #5421 — includes metric & patch. tagging sasha for UX changes.
sasha: will add dashboard panels and change classification in console. also will add a tooltip explaining resume classification.
emily: added alert to paging rules and updated runbook draft.
maya: sounds good. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
alex: follow-up — once canary looks stable, we should backfill missing resume_reason in logs for the 17:22 window for audit.
jonathan: noted — will queue log reindex job after patch.
infra-bot: INC-2026-014 status: triaged -> in_progress.
emily: leaving notes for support and product about UX impact.
alex: great. keep updates here and ping me if there's anything blocking the canary.
